comments.author: @HowDealsWork
comments.text: The quiet logic behind all those brands is that most big hotel companies don't own the buildings. They sell a flag, a booking system and a loyalty programme to owners and earn fees. So when two chains merge, the buyer isn't really paying for real estate. It's paying for fee streams and loyalty members, and each extra brand is another way to sign an owner who would otherwise compete with an existing flag down the street.

Of their brands I found the Hilton Garden inn and Citizen M great value. The room size of the HGI in Downtown Manhattan was excellent for NYC, much better than Double Tree Downtown. The room meant connectivity at Citizen M meant I could connect my streaming apps off my phone straight to the tv in seconds and turn the lights off from the iPad lay in bed, virtually no other hotel offer this. I used CM in DC and LA.I did enjoy the Hyatt Centric Midtown before the price shot up. 
Another Hotel Brand offering a very wide variety of quality is Best Western 

I live in the U.K. and Double Tree is my go to Hilton brand and Novotel my go to Accor Brand though Ibis is great value in Eastern Europe.  

What is missing in the U.S. is Premier Inn, they are the nicest budget brand by far and have a near universal standard bar a few older properties. A lot of the budget brands in the U.S. have very poor standards not helped by the types of people frequenting them e.g. Days Inn.

comments.author: @fluffnbeans
comments.text:
My parents and I lived in Marriott Busan for just over a year and spent a few months in a Renaissance, which I believe changed to Sheraton, in Kuala Lumpur. That was over 20 years ago and the strategy shift is evident when I visit their locations now. Only 4 years after my latest long stay in one of their hotels, I stayed in their Times Sq location and the philosophy had changed a lot. Everything used to be far more thoughtful and almost luxurious back then, especially when you consider the difference between the most expensive and cheapest rooms. I can see the differences even down to how they decorate their desserts nowadays. Cost-cutting I suppose. Long gone are the days when I could go around stealing chocolate covered meringues off all the cakes leaving only one on each so my mother wouldn't yell at me. 

Special shoutout to all the staff who restocked the buffets just to get more dessert decorations out there, the ones who greeted me on my way to/from school and would wait for my parents to come get me, those who came up to our room to tell me when the computer room was free, the cleaning staff who had to cope with my mess and grumpy face becasue I didn't want people touching my things, the restaurant staff who cooked for us at all hours,  and the bar staff who would serve me soft drinks in fancy glasses.

edit: long shot but if you used to work at the Busan location in the early 2000s and remember the italian family living on the top floor (my mom wore big hats), you were family to us and we still have very fond memories of all of you
